title: Exercise 15.2: Limits of Trigonometric Functions
notes: **Topic focus:** Applying trigonometric limits to solve problems.
**Primary tool:** lim(x→0) sin(x)/x = 1 and related standard limits.
**Key technique:** Transform expressions to match standard limit forms using identities.
**Example:** lim(x→0) (1-cos x)/x² = 1/2 using the standard limit.
**Practice source:** Exercise 15.2 with trigonometric limit problems and solutions.
**Connection:** These exercises prepare students for derivative calculations of trig functions.
confusion: Don't forget to adjust the argument: sin(ax)/x needs to become sin(ax)/(ax)·a.
Confusing (1-cos x)/x → 0 with (1-cos x)/x² → 1/2 — the denominator matters.
Forgetting that all trig limits assume radians, not degrees.
Not recognizing when to use which trigonometric identity to transform the expression.
Applying algebraic techniques to trigonometric limits without proper transformation.
practice: Evaluate lim(x→0) sin(5x)/sin(2x) by rewriting in standard form.
Find lim(x→0) (1-cos(2x))/x² using double angle identities.
Evaluate lim(x→0) tan(x)/x² and explain why it doesn't exist.
Find lim(x→0) (sin x - x)/x³ using appropriate trigonometric manipulation.
universalFacts: Trigonometric limit exercises build intuition for the derivatives of sin and cos.
The technique of making substitutions (u = ax) is widely applicable in calculus.
These limits are used in physics to analyze small angle approximations in oscillations.
Mastering these exercises is essential for success in differential calculus.
The same techniques extend to inverse trigonometric function limits.
